owner: CC (code + proofs). Akien owns the rule this is downstream of — "NO GATES MAY CONSULT ORACLES EVER PERIOD. A GATE ONLY OPENS WHEN A FINDINGS LIST IS EMPTY" — and the ruling that opened the sweep, 2026-08-13-everything-always-proved-and-listing-what-it-proved: "EVERYTHING ALWAYS PROVED AND LISTING WHAT IT PROVED", "SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE".
intention: MOVE THE ROUTE SIEVE MESH OUT OF THE COMPONENT THAT DIALS THE HOST, so it can join the proof record like every other gate in the sweep. cairn/devices/inference_domain/route.py holds a six-sieve mesh (enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed, the_nest) plus domain_rows/_finding, and route() returns {"survivors", "gradation", "findings"} with RouteRefused carrying .findings. That findings list is the exact shape the ruling retires: it is empty when every sieve passed AND when a sieve stopped running, so the refusal gate is a gate on SILENCE. The fix is the same one already applied twice in-house: THE SEAM STAYS IN THE DEVICE, THE GATE BERTHS AS A HELD MACHINE — cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route/ — and then the mesh converts to inspect_* returning the proof record, with the findings list surviving as a VIEW over the record's mismatches (derived, never parallel).
why: THIS IS THE ONE PLACE IN THE SWEEP WHERE DOING THE RIGHT THING IN PLACE WOULD MANUFACTURE A VIOLATION. Every other conversion this crossing was `import cairn.tools.gate` plus lanes. Here that single import turns the whole device into a gate that reaches an oracle, because bin/cmd/determinism computes is_gate and llm-reach at COMPONENT granularity and inference_domain's fire path already reaches the LLM. The lived symptom if it is left as it is: Akien opens `cairn determinism` during the sprint he named — "akien can inspect the gates and inspectors and find them deterministic and mostly deterministic respectively, I want to SEE that" — and the sole path to the inference host is the one component whose routing decisions cannot say what they proved. When a request routes to the wrong model, the record says which sieve OBJECTED and never which sieves RAN, so a sieve that quietly stopped firing looks exactly like a request that passed clean.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. "The route mesh found nothing wrong" is today an inference from an empty list, not a measurement of six sieves.

Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics. The no-oracle rule IS physics here (bin/cmd/determinism, gate_violation at determinism.py:309); this ticket is the debt that physics exposed rather than a policy anyone has to remember.
Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces. RouteRefused's .findings is a diagnostic surface and delivers half a diagnosis: the objections, never the attendance.
Law 9 — red is the default. A sieve that stopped running currently reads green.
Ruling 2026-08-13 everything-always-proved-and-listing-what-it-proved — "SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE". This is the named remainder of everywhere.
Ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate — the route mesh is precisely a machine that should carry its own.
gates: The carve-out is done when `./bin/cmd/determinism` lists a NEW row — cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route — as a PURE DETERMINISTIC GATE, while cairn/devices/inference_domain itself still reads REFUSES with NO gate and therefore no gate_violation; and `./bin/cmd/test -q` stays all-green with the route proofs moved beside the machine. The device keeps the seam (domain.py, host.py) and holds the machine; nothing about the dial changes.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) route.py gaining `from cairn.tools.gate import gate` at its CURRENT address — that is the violation this ticket exists to avoid, and bin/cmd/determinism will say so; (2) any lane whose `expected` and `actual` cannot be `==` when it passes — the authoring hazard measured n=4 on 2026-08-13, which reds every HEALTHY subject; the offending value rides in `values`; (3) the findings list surviving as a SECOND implementation rather than a view over the record's mismatches — two mouths for one question is how a gate and the sentence it prints come to disagree; (4) a sieve that did not run appearing in the record as a passing lane rather than being ABSENT — guarded lanes append only when their input is present; (5) the machine's proof roster being HAND-TYPED — a tooth nobody listed is a tooth that did not run, and the file prints the same green line (caught twice on 2026-08-13); (6) the new machine's import surface reaching anything beyond the gate tool and the sieve mesh's own pure dependencies — measure it with an AST tooth like cairn/devices/intention_extractor/machines/judge/proofs/test_judge.py::test_the_judge_holds_no_seam_of_its_own, do not assert it in prose.
horizon: Do it when the sweep's remaining targets are done or when someone is next inside route.py for another reason. It is NOT urgent-in-anger: the mesh is small, stable, and its sieves currently all fire. It IS the last known component blocking the ruling's "everywhere" from being true.
dependencies: MEASURED 2026-08-13, so the size is not a guess. route.py is 264 lines. Its ENTIRE import surface is `json`, `pathlib`, `cairn.tools.base.nest`, `cairn.tools.import_sieve.sieve` — nothing that reaches an oracle. THE MESH IS ALREADY IMPORT-PURE; only its ADDRESS puts it inside a component that dials the host. That is what makes this a MOVE rather than a rewrite.

THE IMPORT EDGE IS ALREADY ONE-WAY AND LAZY, which is what makes the move safe: domain.py:103 `from cairn.devices.inference_domain import route as route_mod   # lazy: keeps import-light` and host.py:307 `# late: keeps the import edge one-way`. route.py imports NEITHER of them. Nothing has to be untangled — the callers are three explicit import lines plus probes/does_a_domain_ride_the_request.py:57, probes/does_the_route_leave_loopback.py:122, proofs/test_route.py:28 and proofs/test_inference_domain.py:122/196/209.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS IT CANNOT BE DONE IN PLACE. cairn/tools/determinism/determinism.py computes `is_gate` from any DIRECT import of cairn.tools.gate anywhere in the component (line ~298) and `gate_violation = is_gate and bool(fire["llm"] or seam["llm"])` (line 309). `./bin/cmd/determinism` today: `! cairn/devices/inference_domain   device   REFUSES / LLM IN THE LOOP: cairn.devices.inference_domain   via cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py`. So the llm half is ALREADY true and unavoidable — inference_domain IS the dial — and the gate half is one import away.

THE PRECEDENT IS IN-HOUSE AND WAS APPLIED THE SAME DAY, so nothing is being invented: cairn/devices/intention_extractor/machines/judge/ was carved out of its device for exactly this reason (its charter's `why` records the determinism violation verbatim), and the builder + skills/chart already berth held machines at devices/<device>/machines/<name>/.

IMPORT_SIEVE'S BAND KEYS ON THE DOTTED PREFIX cairn.devices.inference_domain (sieve.py:90), and the new address cairn.devices.inference_domain.machines.route keeps that prefix — checked on the way in, not assumed.

watchme: none, because the sieve mesh joins the proof record like every other gate — its efficacy is the build inspector's job, not a separate watch
distinctions_recorded: WHICH SIEVES OBJECTED vs WHICH SIEVES RAN. route()'s `findings` is the first and is read as the second. An empty findings list means "nobody objected", which is the ambiguous silence the proof record exists to retire — identical in shape to the a-judge-declares-its-attendance residue, and the same fix.

A GATE'S ADDRESS IS PART OF ITS PHYSICS, NOT ITS FILING. The mesh is already pure; what is impure is living in the same component as the dial. The carve-out changes no logic and yet is the whole fix — which is why 'just add the import' is the wrong-shaped cheap answer here.

THE SEAM STAYS, THE GATE MOVES. This is not a proposal to make inference_domain deterministic — it cannot be and should not be; it IS the oracle's door. It is a proposal to stop a deterministic mesh from borrowing the device's oracle-reach.
filed_edges: THE SIEVE MESH MAY WANT POPULATION LANES, NOT ONLY PASS/FAIL. `route()` shakes a set of COMBOS through six sieves; the settled shape for a collection is expected = the eligible combos, actual = the ones that survived, so a mesh that shrinks to nothing shows an expected of zero rather than an unchanged green. Read the mesh before choosing lane shapes — do not assume six flat boolean lanes.

`the_nest()` READS DISK (cairn.tools.base.nest) and is therefore the one sieve whose lane may be legitimately ABSENT rather than failed when the nest is unreadable. That is the guarded-lane rule, and it is the place this conversion is most likely to author a lane that reds a healthy subject.

DO NOT WIDEN bin/cmd/determinism TO LET THIS PASS. That door was already refused once today on intention_extractor and the refusal was the right call: softening the instrument to fit the code is how the rule stops being physics.
how: Move the route sieve mesh out of cairn/devices/inference_domain/ into a standalone position where it can join the proof record like every other gate in the sweep.
